Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today — good overview of how Medigen captures request/response telemetry for your clinical integration layer. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short proof-of-concept redaction demo: 

- What you said: ELK stores full request/response bodies and headers for 90 days; archived exports are available for audits up to 365 days. Trace IDs and cookies are currently preserved as-is.
- Your ask: show how we would remove or pseudonymize sensitive elements (PII in bodies, Authorization tokens, cookies, trace IDs) while preserving correlation across requests for debugging. Also confirm whether sending sanitized logs off-site satisfies your procurement/compliance teams.

Proposed short plan (attached: redwood_redaction-demo-plan.pdf):
1) We’ll run a synthetic dataset (200 representative requests) through our staging capture and apply two redaction profiles (aggressive/pseudonymize + preserve-debug).
2) Show before/after samples (request/response pairs), including how trace IDs are handled to preserve correlation without leaking raw IDs.
3) Align on retention/sampling settings and provide a written playbook for what stays in logs, what is redacted, and where archived exports live.

Please confirm: 1) we have permission to ingest a small synthetic dataset that mirrors your request shapes (no real PHI), and 2) the right folks to include in the demo (I’ve CC’d you, happy to add security contact).

If that sounds right I’ll loop in our security and infra engineers and propose two demo slots next week.

Hi Monica,

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule:

- Inventory: ELK receives full request/response bodies, request headers (including Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-Id), and response bodies. Retention is 90 days in ELK; exports for legal/audit are stored in S3 for up to 365 days.
- Constraints: our compliance team has said raw Authorization headers cannot leave the prod environment, even to staging (so any demo using real Authorization values is a no-go).
- Question on trace IDs: we use trace IDs to join logs across services and to replay traces into our APM — if they are hashed/pseudonymized, will they still allow the same join behavior?

We can provide a small synthetic sample (no real PHI) and a copy of the security/compliance checklist — attaching that now. Please include details in your playbook about whether pseudonymization is deterministic (so correlation still works) and what key/salt management looks like. Also cc our procurement contact once we have a scope/cost.

Great context — thanks, Sanjay. Looping in Ben (security) and Rishi (infra) from our side to propose the technical approach and confirm constraints. Below is a condensed playbook we intend to demo (also attached: redaction-demo-playbook.md):

Redaction playbook (high level):
- Header rules: allowlist common safe headers (Host, User-Agent), denylist Authorization + Set-Cookie by default. For cookies, we’ll apply a configurable truncation and drop long session tokens.
- Body PII: apply field-level redaction for recognized patterns (SSN, DOB, phone, email) using regex + ML validators.
- Trace IDs: deterministic HMAC-based pseudonymization using a per-customer salt stored in KMS — deterministic so joins/replays still work, non-reversible without the salt. We’ll show a sample before/after to prove correlation.
- Sampling & retention: support tail-sampling and 7/30/90 day buckets; archived exports can be configured to redact further before export.

Proposed demo steps:
1) We run the synthetic dataset you’ll provide in a Redwood staging capture.
2) We apply two redaction profiles ("preserve-debug" — pseudonymize trace IDs, drop auth tokens; "aggressive" — hash trace IDs + mask cookies + remove PII fields).
3) Show live ELK/console view and downloadable sanitized export.

Can you confirm you’ll share the synthetic dataset and a nominal list of request shapes (headers + JSON body examples)? I’ll schedule a 45-minute demo; suggest Thu Feb 13 2–3pm PST or Fri Feb 14 10–11am PST. Once we lock time, Ben/Rishi will prepare the sample sanitized logs and a short runbook for procurement.

Best,
Monica Patel

Hi all — quick techncial confirm from security/infra side. TL;DR: deterministic HMAC pseudonymization + KMS-managed salt is the recommended approach, and it preserves joins while preventing exposure of raw trace IDs. A few implementation details we’ll demo: 

- Pseudonymization details: use HMAC-SHA256(trace_id || customer_salt) and store only the hex prefix (12–16 chars) in searchable indices for performance; the full HMAC can be retained in a secure index if you need full correlation on demand. Deterministic mapping means the same trace_id -> same pseudonym across services.
- Auth headers: we will redact Authorization entirely for off-site exports. For internal staging demo we can substitute synthetic token placeholders; for production exports we recommend token truncation (keep prefix to aid debugging but never the secret part).
- Cookies: identify session cookies by name patterns, drop any cookie values longer than 100 chars, and optionally replace with a stable pseudonym per cookie name+user-id pair.
- KMS/key management: salt stored in customer-owned KMS is preferred; if Medigen prefers Redwood-managed KMS we provide an audit trail and limited access via IAM roles.

Sample sanitized log (for demo purposes only):
{
  "timestamp": "2027-02-10T12:23:45.123Z",
  "request_id_pseudo": "a1f4b2c9d7e3",
  "method": "POST",
  "path": "/api/v1/patient",
  "request_headers": {
    "Host": "api.medigen.com",
    "User-Agent": "MedigenClient/3.2.1",
    "X-Trace-Id": "a1f4b2c9d7e3",
    "Authorization": "REDACTED"
  },
  "request_body_sanitized": {
    "patient_id": "REDACTED",
    "dob": "REDACTED",
    "symptoms": "fever, cough"
  }
}

Next steps: 1) Sanjay — please drop the synthetic dataset (zip) at the drive link above or confirm we should generate synthetic traffic from your shape examples; 2) Monica — pick one of the proposed demo slots and I’ll prepare the redaction configs; 3) We’ll include a brief procurement note on cost/effort after the demo if Medigen wants a production rollout.

Happy to go deeper on any of the items in the playbook during the demo.

— Ben
